column10: Confirmed by the lead directly in the retained article text, independently of the two auditor agents (A2 and E1) that raised it, and this is guidance §15.1(2) exactly — a relative anchor that exists but measures to the wrong point. MECHANISM, STATED CORRECTLY: a `relative` date in this corpus carries only {of, statement, note} — scripts/_chronology.py:1295 rejects any other key — so there is NO signed magnitude and NOTHING COMPUTES from it. The 367 lives only in the prose `statement` and `label`. The harm is therefore not a compounding arithmetic but a false displayed claim: a consumer asking about israel.patriarchs.birth-of-abram is told '367 years from the flood, in the Hebrew', which the source says of the CALL. That is still a wrong fact reaching a consumer under this profile, and the corpus separately holds the call at +75 from the birth on Genesis 12:4, so the two stored statements cannot both be true. guidance §10.0 already records this constraint about the class as a whole — 'Nothing computed with them, which is the only reason no wrong date had yet been produced.' column10: Three defects at once. (1) The stored relative.statement is not in the source: its clauses have been reordered so that the four hundred and fifty years attach to the judges, which is precisely the attachment the claim's own note says the Douay does NOT make ('The Douay punctuation attaches the four hundred and fifty years to what precedes'). A quotation the source does not contain is failure mode 15.1(1). (2) The anchor israel.monarchy.saul-accession exists but is measured from by nothing in the passage; combined with the label's direction word 'after', the claim resolves to the period of the Judges standing four hundred and fifty years AFTER the founding of the monarchy, and israel.monarchy.saul-accession carries an absolute year (1020 B.C.), so a resolver produces a materially false date. (3) The subject's own subject_note contradicts the claim: 'The two figures the tracked Douay text carries are both durations' - yet the claim is stored as relative. Removal is recommended because the tracked Douay supports neither structure for this subject: not a duration of the judges (the figure precedes them) and not an offset (no anchor is named). If the figure is retained it must be re-subjected to the span of Acts 13:17-19 and never anchored on Saul. A separate wrong-anchor row is filed as A2-029.

Note this is NOT the same as the query API answering at any verse number: `tools/tpt scripture-chronology query Gen.1.99` also answers, so verse-existence is not checked anywhere and that is a general property, not a native-scope defect. The defect here is the counted universe.

column9: Keep the loader fix, drop the scope fix, and reverse the stated harm. Section 3.0's gate exists, in its own docstring's words, to stop an author placing at a native scope 'a fact that the Vulgate already holds and that the concordance can safely carry between them'. composition.book-of-ecclesiasticus.greek holds no such fact: it holds the date of the GREEK TRANSLATION (about 132 B.C.), which the Vulgate unit does not hold and says it does not hold, so the gate's purpose is not breached and only its literal formulation is over-broad. Narrowing the Greek scope to exclude 36:16, as the finding recommends, would strip from that locus the one assertion that is actually true of it. The consumer-visible effect is the opposite of the one the finding describes: I confirmed with tools/tpt scripture-chronology query Ecclus.36.16 --system greek --json that the answer is mapping status shared, reached Ecclus.36.18, carrying the Vulgate unit's 190-170 B.C. and 280 B.C. and NOT the Greek translation's 132 B.C. - so no duplicate is served, a true native assertion is discarded, which is 15.1(9)'s family inverted. Correct remedy: either have the gate test for a duplicated FACT rather than a shareable locus, or make the resolve path return a native assertion alongside the shared one when both exist. No stored date changes, and the factual result reaching a consumer is unchanged today, which is why this is minor. The lead's corrections of N-006 (not critical) and N-007 (1 356 printed, not 1 391) are both independently confirmed.
column10: This CORRECTS the class-N auditor's N-006, which rated the same defect `critical` on the ground that the query 'answers about the wrong text there'. No wrong date reaches a consumer, so this is major (a gate that does not enforce the rule it exists for), not critical. The class-D auditor's D-004 states the same fact correctly: the native assertion is computed and then discarded when the mapping succeeds. ALSO CORRECTED HERE: N-007 states that "the Greek Ecclesiasticus prints 1 391 loci". It prints 1 356. 1 391 is the densified figure produced by the _system_loci defect in LEAD-011; the repository's own _chronology.py docstring and composition.yaml both say "1 355 of its 1 356 loci" and are right, while guidance §3.0.1 and §9.3 carry the inflated figure. The lead recommended narrowing the scope; verification showed that would delete the one assertion true of greek 36:16, since the Greek unit holds the translation's date and the Vulgate unit holds the Hebrew original's.
